questions.stem: In the context of computer networking, what does the acronym 'URL' stand for?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. It is the global address of documents and other resources on the World Wide Web. It specifies the location of a web resource on a computer network and the mechanism (like HTTP or FTP) used to retrieve it.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Universal Routing Link' sounds technical but is made up. Remember 'Uniform', not 'Universal' or 'Unified'.
EXAM INSIGHT: A URL is a specific type of URI (Uniform Resource Identifier). The first part (http://) is the protocol, and the second part (www.example.com) is the domain name or IP address.

questions.stem: Which of the following network topologies connects all devices to a single central cable, known as the backbone?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: In a Bus Topology, all nodes (computers, printers, etc.) are connected to a single central cable, called the bus or backbone. If the main cable fails, the entire network shuts down.
DECOY BUSTING: Star topology connects all devices to a central hub/switch. Ring topology connects devices in a closed loop. Mesh topology connects every device to every other device.
EXAM INSIGHT: Bus topology was very common in early Ethernet networks but is rarely used today due to its single point of failure.
